action.description: Action object MUST contain a field `submission`, and MAY contain arbitrary additional information.

actTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) to obtain an action from an agent.

episodeSteps.description: Maximum number of steps in the episode.

includeLegalActions.description: If true, include legalActions and legalActionStrings in observations. Defaults to false since these can be derived from serializedGameAndState.

initialActions.description: Actions applied to initial state before play begins to set up starting position.

loadPresetHands.description: Repeated poker only. Load preset hand chance actions from preset_hands.jsonl.

openSpielGameName.description: The short_name of the OpenSpiel game to load.

openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

action.thoughts:
### Reasoning
The board is 6 rows by 7 columns, with rows indexed 0 (top) to 5 (bottom). The current state has an X in row 5, column 3, and an O in row 4, column 3. All other positions are empty. As player X, it's my turn.

This position arose from X's first move in the center (column 3), followed by O stacking on top—a suboptimal move by O, as it doesn't create threats or block effectively. Stacking another X in column 3 (to row 3) would place X on top of O, resulting in X-O-X vertically, but the X's are not connected, and it doesn't create an immediate threat. Analysis shows this allows O to ignore the column for two turns, build elsewhere, and block only when necessary, preventing X from getting 4 in a row vertically without gaining advantage.

Instead, the optimal move is to play in an adjacent column at the bottom to create a connected pair of X's horizontally in row 5. This builds a stronger foundation for future horizontal, diagonal, or vertical threats, exploiting O's weak response and forcing O into defensive plays sooner. Columns 2 and 4 are symmetric and equivalent in this regard. I select column 4 for this move, as it maintains centrality and sets up potential for quick forcing sequences (e.g., building toward an open three-in-a-row).

This move aligns with perfect play in Connect Four, where exploiting a stacked center by playing adjacent leads to a win for the first player.

Final Answer: 4

The current board state, with rows numbered 0 (top) to 5 (bottom), shows player X with pieces at row 5, columns 3 and 4. Player O has pieces at row 3, column 3 and row 4, column 3. No player has 4 in a row yet.

No move allows X to win immediately, as adding one piece to the existing two X's cannot form 4 in a row.

However, dropping in column 2 places an X at row 5, column 2, creating three X's horizontally in row 5, columns 2-4. This threatens a win on the next turn by dropping in column 1 (forming 4 in row 5, columns 1-4) or column 5 (forming 4 in row 5, columns 2-5). O can block only one threat, allowing X to win on the following turn.

O cannot win immediately after this move, as O's two pieces are vertical, and adding one piece can at most form three in a row (by dropping in column 3), not four. Any other O move also fails to form four.

Dropping in column 5 is similarly optimal (creating three in row 5, columns 3-5, threatening columns 2 or 6), but column 2 is selected as it is equally forcing and closer to the center.
